elements.id-string-13: Electronic structure elucidation is a hard problem for conventional computation, due to the super-exponential scaling of the Hilbert space with the physical size of the system.
elements.id-string-14: Quantum computers have been heralded as a solution to this problem,\cite{Feynman1982, Aspuru-Guzik2005} mainly due to their ability to use the quantum entanglement of their constituent qubits to encode even highly complex electronic wavefunctions in a linearly scaling qubit register.

elements.id-string-16: However, while these techniques promise clean, general solutions to many problems in quantum chemistry, they require many-qubit, fully fault-tolerant quantum computers to run.
elements.id-string-17: Currently we are in an era of Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum (NISQ) hardware,\cite{Preskill2018} which is characterised by moderate numbers (10 -- 1000) of qubits prone to high error rates, due to short coherence times and noisy gate implementations.\cite{Linke2017} While significant work is being carried out in the fields of quantum error correction\cite{Georgescu2020} and mitigation, \cite{Cai2022} the fully fault-tolerant quantum computer remains a thing of the future.
